[user]
=== Three Pigs: Secret Materials ===

Materials are Straw, Wood and Brick. The locations are []: Fields gives Straw, Forest gives Wood, Brickyard gives Brick. Each pile starts at 0.

Each player is secretly dealt a Favoured Material. With 3 players one Straw, one Wood and one Brick card are shuffled and dealt, so all three differ; with 4 players two of each are shuffled and one dealt to each, and the undealt cards stay hidden. Your Favoured Material is known only to you. Everyone starts with 0 Straw, Wood and Brick; your stockpile is private.

HOUSES: a house is one material and has 3 sections, built in order: Floor, Walls, Roof. Each section costs 2 of that house's material, or 1 if it is your Favoured Material. You may have at most 1 unfinished house of each material, and may complete at most 2 houses of any one material. Which sections each player has built, and of what material, is public; the cost paid is not shown.

EACH ROUND (up to 15 rounds):
1. Bonus: one location is drawn at random (each 1/3) and announced.
2. Refill: every pile gains 3, and the bonus location gains 2 more.
3. Talk: everyone writes one short message at the same time; all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one.
4. Gather choice: everyone simultaneously chooses one of Fields, Forest, Brickyard, Market, Wolf-Fields, Wolf-Forest, Wolf-Brickyard.
5. Reveal: all choices are shown.
6. Resolve each location: if any player chose Wolf at that location, nobody gathers there and its pile is unchanged. Otherwise the pile is divided equally among the players who chose it, rounding down; each takes their share and the remainder stays in the pile (5 split by 2 gives each 2 and leaves 1). If nobody chose a location, its pile stays and carries over. Each player is told only their own gain, but the piles and the numbers of gatherers and wolves are public.
7. Market: every player who chose Market gains 1 of their Favoured Material, however many others chose Market.
8. Players who chose a Wolf gain nothing.
9. Build action 1: everyone simultaneously chooses Build Straw, Build Wood, Build Brick or Pass. A build adds the next section to your house of that material, starting a new house at the Floor if none is unfinished, and pays the cost from your stockpile. If you cannot pay, or the build would start a third house of that material, it counts as Pass and nothing changes; you are only offered the builds you can make, and Pass is always offered. When a Roof is built the house is complete. The public build state is then shown.
10. Build action 2: exactly as build action 1 (2 build actions per round).
11. Win check: any player with 3 completed houses has finished. If exactly one player has finished, they win. If several have, the finisher with the most total leftover resources (Straw + Wood + Brick) wins; if that is tied, it is a draw among them. The game then ends.

1. Bonus: one location is drawn at random (each 1/3) and announced.

Otherwise the pile is divided equally among the players who chose it, rounding down; each takes their share and the remainder stays in the pile (5 split by 2 gives each 2 and leaves 1). 1. Bonus: one location is drawn at random (each 1/3) and announced.
2. Refill: every pile gains 3, and the bonus location gains 2 more.
3. Talk: everyone writes one short message at the same time; all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one.

Otherwise the pile is divided equally among the players who chose it, rounding down; each takes their share and the remainder stays in the pile (5 split by 2 gives each 2 and leaves 1). [user]
=== Three Pigs: Secret Materials ===

Materials are Straw, Wood and Brick. The locations are []: Fields gives Straw, Forest gives Wood, Brickyard gives Brick. Each pile starts at 0.

Each player is secretly dealt a Favoured Material. With 3 players one Straw, one Wood and one Brick card are shuffled and dealt, so all three differ; with 4 players two of each are shuffled and one dealt to each, and the undealt cards stay hidden. Your Favoured Material is known only to you. Everyone starts with 0 Straw, Wood and Brick; your stockpile is private.

HOUSES: a house is one material and has 3 sections, built in order: Floor, Walls, Roof. Each section costs 2 of that house's material, or 1 if it is your Favoured Material. You may have at most 1 unfinished house of each material, and may complete at most 2 houses of any one material. Which sections each player has built, and of what material, is public; the cost paid is not shown.

EACH ROUND (up to 15 rounds):
1. Bonus: one location is drawn at random (each 1/3) and announced.
2. Refill: every pile gains 3, and the bonus location gains 2 more.
3. Talk: everyone writes one short message at the same time; all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one.
4. Gather choice: everyone simultaneously chooses one of Fields, Forest, Brickyard, Market, Wolf-Fields, Wolf-Forest, Wolf-Brickyard.
5. Reveal: all choices are shown.
6. Resolve each location: if any player chose Wolf at that location, nobody gathers there and its pile is unchanged. Otherwise the pile is divided equally among the players who chose it, rounding down; each takes their share and the remainder stays in the pile (5 split by 2 gives each 2 and leaves 1). If nobody chose a location, its pile stays and carries over. Each player is told only their own gain, but the piles and the numbers of gatherers and wolves are public.
7. Market: every player who chose Market gains 1 of their Favoured Material, however many others chose Market.
8. Players who chose a Wolf gain nothing.
9. Build action 1: everyone simultaneously chooses Build Straw, Build Wood, Build Brick or Pass. A build adds the next section to your house of that material, starting a new house at the Floor if none is unfinished, and pays the cost from your stockpile. If you cannot pay, or the build would start a third house of that material, it counts as Pass and nothing changes; you are only offered the builds you can make, and Pass is always offered. When a Roof is built the house is complete. The public build state is then shown.
10. Build action 2: exactly as build action 1 (2 build actions per round).
11. Win check: any player with 3 completed houses has finished. If exactly one player has finished, they win. If several have, the finisher with the most total leftover resources (Straw + Wood + Brick) wins; if that is tied, it is a draw among them. The game then ends.

[user]
=== Three Pigs: Secret Materials ===

Materials are Straw, Wood and Brick. The locations are []: Fields gives Straw, Forest gives Wood, Brickyard gives Brick. Each pile starts at 0.

Each player is secretly dealt a Favoured Material. With 3 players one Straw, one Wood and one Brick card are shuffled and dealt, so all three differ; with 4 players two of each are shuffled and one dealt to each, and the undealt cards stay hidden. Your Favoured Material is known only to you. Everyone starts with 0 Straw, Wood and Brick; your stockpile is private.

HOUSES: a house is one material and has 3 sections, built in order: Floor, Walls, Roof. Each section costs 2 of that house's material, or 1 if it is your Favoured Material. You may have at most 1 unfinished house of each material, and may complete at most 2 houses of any one material. Which sections each player has built, and of what material, is public; the cost paid is not shown.

EACH ROUND (up to 15 rounds):
1. Bonus: one location is drawn at random (each 1/3) and announced.
2. Refill: every pile gains 3, and the bonus location gains 2 more.
3. Talk: everyone writes one short message at the same time; all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one.
4. Gather choice: everyone simultaneously chooses one of Fields, Forest, Brickyard, Market, Wolf-Fields, Wolf-Forest, Wolf-Brickyard.
5. Reveal: all choices are shown.
6. Resolve each location: if any player chose Wolf at that location, nobody gathers there and its pile is unchanged. Otherwise the pile is divided equally among the players who chose it, rounding down; each takes their share and the remainder stays in the pile (5 split by 2 gives each 2 and leaves 1). If nobody chose a location, its pile stays and carries over. Each player is told only their own gain, but the piles and the numbers of gatherers and wolves are public.
7. Market: every player who chose Market gains 1 of their Favoured Material, however many others chose Market.
8. Players who chose a Wolf gain nothing.
9. Build action 1: everyone simultaneously chooses Build Straw, Build Wood, Build Brick or Pass. A build adds the next section to your house of that material, starting a new house at the Floor if none is unfinished, and pays the cost from your stockpile. If you cannot pay, or the build would start a third house of that material, it counts as Pass and nothing changes; you are only offered the builds you can make, and Pass is always offered. When a Roof is built the house is complete. The public build state is then shown.
10. Build action 2: exactly as build action 1 (2 build actions per round).
11. Win check: any player with 3 completed houses has finished. If exactly one player has finished, they win. If several have, the finisher with the most total leftover resources (Straw + Wood + Brick) wins; if that is tied, it is a draw among them. The game then ends.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Three Pigs: Secret Materials ===

Materials are Straw, Wood and Brick. The locations are []: Fields gives Straw, Forest gives Wood, Brickyard gives Brick. Each pile starts at 0.

Each player is secretly dealt a Favoured Material. With 3 players one Straw, one Wood and one Brick card are shuffled and dealt, so all three differ; with 4 players two of each are shuffled and one dealt to each, and the undealt cards stay hidden. Your Favoured Material is known only to you. Everyone starts with 0 Straw, Wood and Brick; your stockpile is private.

HOUSES: a house is one material and has 3 sections, built in order: Floor, Walls, Roof. Each section costs 2 of that house's material, or 1 if it is your Favoured Material. You may have at most 1 unfinished house of each material, and may complete at most 2 houses of any one material. Which sections each player has built, and of what material, is public; the cost paid is not shown.

EACH ROUND (up to 15 rounds):
1. Bonus: one location is drawn at random (each 1/3) and announced.
2. Refill: every pile gains 3, and the bonus location gains 2 more.
3. Talk: everyone writes one short message at the same time; all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one.
4. Gather choice: everyone simultaneously chooses one of Fields, Forest, Brickyard, Market, Wolf-Fields, Wolf-Forest, Wolf-Brickyard.
5. Reveal: all choices are shown.
6. Resolve each location: if any player chose Wolf at that location, nobody gathers there and its pile is unchanged. Otherwise the pile is divided equally among the players who chose it, rounding down; each takes their share and the remainder stays in the pile (5 split by 2 gives each 2 and leaves 1). If nobody chose a location, its pile stays and carries over. Each player is told only their own gain, but the piles and the numbers of gatherers and wolves are public.
7. Market: every player who chose Market gains 1 of their Favoured Material, however many others chose Market.
8. Players who chose a Wolf gain nothing.
9. Build action 1: everyone simultaneously chooses Build Straw, Build Wood, Build Brick or Pass. A build adds the next section to your house of that material, starting a new house at the Floor if none is unfinished, and pays the cost from your stockpile. If you cannot pay, or the build would start a third house of that material, it counts as Pass and nothing changes; you are only offered the builds you can make, and Pass is always offered. When a Roof is built the house is complete. The public build state is then shown.
10. Build action 2: exactly as build action 1 (2 build actions per round).
11. Win check: any player with 3 completed houses has finished. If exactly one player has finished, they win. If several have, the finisher with the most total leftover resources (Straw + Wood + Brick) wins; if that is tied, it is a draw among them. The game then ends.
12. If round 15 ends with no finisher, the game ends: the player with the most completed houses wins, then the most built sections; if still tied, it is a draw.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Three Pigs: Secret Materials ===

Materials are Straw, Wood and Brick. The locations are []: Fields gives Straw, Forest gives Wood, Brickyard gives Brick. Each pile starts at 0.

Each player is secretly dealt a Favoured Material. With 3 players one Straw, one Wood and one Brick card are shuffled and dealt, so all three differ; with 4 players two of each are shuffled and one dealt to each, and the undealt cards stay hidden. Your Favoured Material is known only to you. Everyone starts with 0 Straw, Wood and Brick; your stockpile is private.

HOUSES: a house is one material and has 3 sections, built in order: Floor, Walls, Roof. Each section costs 2 of that house's material, or 1 if it is your Favoured Material. You may have at most 1 unfinished house of each material, and may complete at most 2 houses of any one material. Which sections each player has built, and of what material, is public; the cost paid is not shown.

EACH ROUND (up to 15 rounds):
1. Bonus: one location is drawn at random (each 1/3) and announced.
2. Refill: every pile gains 3, and the bonus location gains 2 more.
3. Talk: everyone writes one short message at the same time; all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one.
4. Gather choice: everyone simultaneously chooses one of Fields, Forest, Brickyard, Market, Wolf-Fields, Wolf-Forest, Wolf-Brickyard.
5. Reveal: all choices are shown.
6. Resolve each location: if any player chose Wolf at that location, nobody gathers there and its pile is unchanged. Otherwise the pile is divided equally among the players who chose it, rounding down; each takes their share and the remainder stays in the pile (5 split by 2 gives each 2 and leaves 1). If nobody chose a location, its pile stays and carries over. Each player is told only their own gain, but the piles and the numbers of gatherers and wolves are public.
7. Market: every player who chose Market gains 1 of their Favoured Material, however many others chose Market.
8. Players who chose a Wolf gain nothing.
9. Build action 1: everyone simultaneously chooses Build Straw, Build Wood, Build Brick or Pass. A build adds the next section to your house of that material, starting a new house at the Floor if none is unfinished, and pays the cost from your stockpile. If you cannot pay, or the build would start a third house of that material, it counts as Pass and nothing changes; you are only offered the builds you can make, and Pass is always offered. When a Roof is built the house is complete. The public build state is then shown.
10. Build action 2: exactly as build action 1 (2 build actions per round).
11. Win check: any player with 3 completed houses has finished. If exactly one player has finished, they win. If several have, the finisher with the most total leftover resources (Straw + Wood + Brick) wins; if that is tied, it is a draw among them. The game then ends.

Your Favoured Material is known only to you. Everyone starts with 0 Straw, Wood and Brick; your stockpile is private.

HOUSES: a house is one material and has 3 sections, built in order: Floor, Walls, Roof. Each section costs 2 of that house's material, or 1 if it is your Favoured Material. You may have at most 1 unfinished house of each material, and may complete at most 2 houses of any one material. 1. Bonus: one location is drawn at random (each 1/3) and announced.
2. Refill: every pile gains 3, and the bonus location gains 2 more.
3. Talk: everyone writes one short message at the same time; all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one.

[user]
=== Three Pigs: Secret Materials ===

Materials are Straw, Wood and Brick. The locations are []: Fields gives Straw, Forest gives Wood, Brickyard gives Brick. Each pile starts at 0.

Each player is secretly dealt a Favoured Material. With 3 players one Straw, one Wood and one Brick card are shuffled and dealt, so all three differ; with 4 players two of each are shuffled and one dealt to each, and the undealt cards stay hidden. Your Favoured Material is known only to you. Everyone starts with 0 Straw, Wood and Brick; your stockpile is private.

HOUSES: a house is one material and has 3 sections, built in order: Floor, Walls, Roof. Each section costs 2 of that house's material, or 1 if it is your Favoured Material. You may have at most 1 unfinished house of each material, and may complete at most 2 houses of any one material. Which sections each player has built, and of what material, is public; the cost paid is not shown.

EACH ROUND (up to 15 rounds):
1. Bonus: one location is drawn at random (each 1/3) and announced.
2. Refill: every pile gains 3, and the bonus location gains 2 more.
3. Talk: everyone writes one short message at the same time; all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one.
4. Gather choice: everyone simultaneously chooses one of Fields, Forest, Brickyard, Market, Wolf-Fields, Wolf-Forest, Wolf-Brickyard.
5. Reveal: all choices are shown.
6. Resolve each location: if any player chose Wolf at that location, nobody gathers there and its pile is unchanged. Otherwise the pile is divided equally among the players who chose it, rounding down; each takes their share and the remainder stays in the pile (5 split by 2 gives each 2 and leaves 1). If nobody chose a location, its pile stays and carries over. Each player is told only their own gain, but the piles and the numbers of gatherers and wolves are public.
7. Market: every player who chose Market gains 1 of their Favoured Material, however many others chose Market.
8. Players who chose a Wolf gain nothing.
9. Build action 1: everyone simultaneously chooses Build Straw, Build Wood, Build Brick or Pass. A build adds the next section to your house of that material, starting a new house at the Floor if none is unfinished, and pays the cost from your stockpile. If you cannot pay, or the build would start a third house of that material, it counts as Pass and nothing changes; you are only offered the builds you can make, and Pass is always offered. When a Roof is built the house is complete. The public build state is then shown.
10. Build action 2: exactly as build action 1 (2 build actions per round).
11. Win check: any player with 3 completed houses has finished. If exactly one player has finished, they win. If several have, the finisher with the most total leftover resources (Straw + Wood + Brick) wins; if that is tied, it is a draw among them. The game then ends.

records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
Materials are Straw, Wood and Brick. The locations are []: Fields gives Straw, Forest gives Wood, Brickyard gives Brick. Each pile starts at 0.

Each player is secretly dealt a Favoured Material. With 3 players one Straw, one Wood and one Brick card are shuffled and dealt, so all three differ; with 4 players two of each are shuffled and one dealt to each, and the undealt cards stay hidden. Your Favoured Material is known only to you. Everyone starts with 0 Straw, Wood and Brick; your stockpile is private.

HOUSES: a house is one material and has 3 sections, built in order: Floor, Walls, Roof. Each section costs 2 of that house's material, or 1 if it is your Favoured Material. You may have at most 1 unfinished house of each material, and may complete at most 2 houses of any one material. Which sections each player has built, and of what material, is public; the cost paid is not shown.

EACH ROUND (up to 15 rounds):
1. Bonus: one location is drawn at random (each 1/3) and announced.
2. Refill: every pile gains 3, and the bonus location gains 2 more.
3. Talk: everyone writes one short message at the same time; all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one.
4. Gather choice: everyone simultaneously chooses one of Fields, Forest, Brickyard, Market, Wolf-Fields, Wolf-Forest, Wolf-Brickyard.
5. Reveal: all choices are shown.
6. Resolve each location: if any player chose Wolf at that location, nobody gathers there and its pile is unchanged. Otherwise the pile is divided equally among the players who chose it, rounding down; each takes their share and the remainder stays in the pile (5 split by 2 gives each 2 and leaves 1). If nobody chose a location, its pile stays and carries over. Each player is told only their own gain, but the piles and the numbers of gatherers and wolves are public.
7. Market: every player who chose Market gains 1 of their Favoured Material, however many others chose Market.
8. Players who chose a Wolf gain nothing.
9. Build action 1: everyone simultaneously chooses Build Straw, Build Wood, Build Brick or Pass. A build adds the next section to your house of that material, starting a new house at the Floor if none is unfinished, and pays the cost from your stockpile. If you cannot pay, or the build would start a third house of that material, it counts as Pass and nothing changes; you are only offered the builds you can make, and Pass is always offered. When a Roof is built the house is complete. The public build state is then shown.
10. Build action 2: exactly as build action 1 (2 build actions per round).
11. Win check: any player with 3 completed houses has finished. If exactly one player has finished, they win. If several have, the finisher with the most total leftover resources (Straw + Wood + Brick) wins; if that is tied, it is a draw among them. The game then ends.
12. If round 15 ends with no finisher, the game ends: the player with the most completed houses wins, then the most built sections; if still tied, it is a draw.
